chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Basir from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Among the perfection of fasting is giving the zakat, just as sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is among the perfection of the prayer.
And whoever fasts and does not pay it, there is no fast for him if he leaves it deliberately.
And whoever prays and does not send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and leaves that deliberately, there is no prayer for him.
Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, began with it before the prayer, saying:
He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself and mentions the name of his Lord and prays.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between paying zakat and the validity of fasting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the intrinsic link between spiritual purification (zakat) and ritual worship, framing zakat not merely as a financial duty but as a perfection of the fast. The analogy to *Salat al-Nabi* highlights the Shia emphasis on voluntary blessings as integral to the completeness of prayer, while the condition of 'deliberate neglect' (*muta'ammidan*) distinguishes between minor omission and the nullification of the act. This reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential view that zakat serves as the spiritual cleansing that validates the physical discipline of fasting.
